title: Frontend: Nested Checkbox
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Nested Checkbox. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({tree={id:root,label:All,children:[{id:a,label:A},{id:b,label:B}]}}). Render a checkbox[data-node=ID] for every tree node. Leaves own selection. A parent toggles all descendant leaves; derive checked/mixed/unchecked in data-state and set actual indeterminate property for mixed state. Empty branches are treated as leaves. [data-testid=selected] is sorted selected leaf IDs comma-joined.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store selected leaves or an equivalent normalized model.
alternativeApproaches: Support lazy-loaded children without incorrectly declaring an incompletely known subtree fully selected.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: All/none/some leaves; disabled descendant; empty branch.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
